metadata.fold_exclusion_rule: For each training target, exclude all 16 documents in its heldout fold from vectorizer fitting and retrieval; A targets use all 80 training documents.
metadata.query_rule: TF-IDF uses only original full_text; target gold entities and associations are never used. Candidate HPO IDs come only from supplied CPU prediction snapshots.
metadata.example_rule: Retrieve the top two documents by text cosine similarity only. Include an example only if its training gold association overlaps target predicted HPO IDs and has non-negated entity evidence. No replacement by lower-ranked documents.
metadata.evidence_rule: Gold patient-phenotype labels are authoritative; the nearby phenotype window illustrates original wording and is not separately annotated pair-level evidence.

HP:0000967.definition: Petechiae are pinpoint-sized reddish/purple spots, resembling a rash, that appear just under the skin or a mucous membrane when capillaries have ruptured and some superficial bleeding into the skin has happened. HP:0001903.name: Anemia

HP:0001954.name: Recurrent fever

HP:0001992.name: Organic aciduria
HP:0001992.definition: Excretion of non-amino organic acids in urine.

HP:0002104.name: Apnea
HP:0002104.definition: Lack of breathing with no movement of the respiratory muscles and no exchange of air in the lungs. This term refers to a disposition to have recurrent episodes of apnea rather than to a single event.

HP:0000407.definition: A type of hearing impairment in one or both ears related to an abnormal functionality of the cochlear nerve.

HP:0000218.name: High palate
HP:0000218.definition: Height of the palate more than 2 SD above the mean (objective) or palatal height at the level of the first permanent molar more than twice the height of the teeth (subjective).

HP:0000508.name: Ptosis
HP:0000508.definition: The upper eyelid margin is positioned 3 mm or more lower than usual and covers the superior portion of the iris (objective); or, the upper lid margin obscures at least part of the pupil (subjective).

HP:0001265.name: Hyporeflexia
HP:0001265.definition: Reduction of neurologic reflexes such as the knee-jerk reaction.

HP:0001649.name: Tachycardia
HP:0001649.definition: A rapid heartrate that exceeds the range of the normal resting heartrate for age.

HP:0001762.name: Talipes equinovarus
HP:0001762.definition: Talipes equinovarus (also called clubfoot) typically has four main components: inversion and adduction of the forefoot; inversion of the heel and hindfoot; equinus (limitation of extension) of the ankle and subtalar joint; and internal rotation of the leg.

HP:0001942.name: Metabolic acidosis
HP:0001942.definition: Metabolic acidosis (MA) is characterized by a fall in blood pH due to a reduction of serum bicarbonate concentration. This can occur as a result of either the accumulation of acids (high anion gap MA) or the loss of bicarbonate from the gastrointestinal tract or the kidney (hyperchloremic MA). By de

HP:0001945.name: Fever
HP:0001945.definition: Body temperature elevated above the normal range.

HP:0001999.name: Abnormal facial shape
HP:0001999.definition: An abnormal morphology (form) of the face or its components.

HP:0002047.name: Malignant hyperthermia
HP:0002047.definition: Malignant hyperthermia is characterized by a rapid increase in temperature to 39-42 degrees C. Malignant hyperthermia may occur in response to either inhalational anesthetics such as halothane, to muscle relaxants such as succinylcholine, or to exercise.

HP:0002063.name: Rigidity
HP:0002063.definition: Continuous involuntary sustained muscle contraction. When an affected muscle is passively stretched, the degree of resistance remains constant regardless of the rate at which the muscle is stretched. This feature helps to distinguish rigidity from muscle spasticity.

HP:0002153.name: Hyperkalemia
HP:0002153.definition: The concentration of potassium(1+) in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

HP:0002789.name: Tachypnea
synonyms: Increased respiratory rate or depth of breathing

HP:0002808.name: Kyphosis
HP:0002808.definition: Exaggerated anterior convexity of the thoracic vertebral column.

HP:0003198.name: Myopathy
HP:0003198.definition: A disorder of muscle unrelated to impairment of innervation or neuromuscular junction.

HP:0003201.name: Rhabdomyolysis
HP:0003201.definition: Breakdown of muscle fibers that leads to the release of muscle fiber contents (myoglobin) into the bloodstream.

HP:0003546.name: Exercise intolerance
HP:0003546.definition: A functional motor deficit where individuals whose responses to the challenges of exercise fail to achieve levels considered normal for their age and gender.

HP:0012416.name: Hypercapnia
HP:0012416.definition: Abnormally elevated blood carbon dioxide (CO2) level.

HP:0034392.name: Joint contracture
HP:0034392.definition: A limitation in the passive range of motion of a joint resulting from loss of elasticity in the periarticular tissues owing to structural changes of non-bony tissues, such as muscles, tendons, ligaments, joint capsules or skin. A contracture prevents movement of the associated body part.

HP:0041219.name: Elbow fracture
HP:0041219.definition: A partial or complete breakage of the elbow.

HP:0000103.name: Polyuria
HP:0000103.definition: An increased rate of urine production.

HP:0000217.name: Xerostomia
HP:0000217.definition: Dryness of the mouth due to salivary gland dysfunction.

HP:0000365.name: Hearing impairment
HP:0000365.definition: A decreased magnitude of the sensory perception of sound.

HP:0000407.name: Sensorineural hearing impairment
HP:0000407.definition: A type of hearing impairment in one or both ears related to an abnormal functionality of the cochlear nerve.

HP:0000488.name: Retinopathy
HP:0000488.definition: Any noninflammatory disease of the retina. This nonspecific term is retained here because of its wide use in the literature, but if possible new annotations should indicate the precise type of retinal abnormality.

HP:0000505.name: Visual impairment
HP:0000505.definition: Visual impairment (or vision impairment) is vision loss (of a person) to such a degree as to qualify as an additional support need through a significant limitation of visual capability resulting from either disease, trauma, or congenital or degenerative conditions that cannot be corrected by convent

HP:0000572.name: Visual loss
HP:0000572.definition: Loss of visual acuity (implying that vision was better at a certain time point in life). Otherwise the term reduced visual acuity should be used (or a subclass of that).

HP:0000622.name: Blurred vision
HP:0000622.definition: Lack of sharpness of vision resulting in the inability to see fine detail.

HP:0000648.name: Optic atrophy
HP:0000648.definition: Atrophy of the optic nerve. Optic atrophy results from the death of the retinal ganglion cell axons that comprise the optic nerve and manifesting as a pale optic nerve on fundoscopy.

HP:0000819.name: Diabetes mellitus
HP:0000819.definition: A group of abnormalities characterized by hyperglycemia and glucose intolerance.

HP:0000855.name: Insulin resistance
HP:0000855.definition: Increased resistance towards insulin, that is, diminished effectiveness of insulin in reducing blood glucose levels.
synonyms: Body fails to respond to insulin

HP:0000873.name: Diabetes insipidus
HP:0000873.definition: A state of excessive water intake and hypotonic (dilute) polyuria. Diabetes insipidus may be due to failure of vasopressin (AVP) release (central or neurogenic diabetes insipidus) or to a failure of the kidney to respond to AVP (nephrogenic diabetes insipidus).

HP:0001943.name: Hypoglycemia
HP:0001943.definition: A decreased concentration of glucose in the blood.

HP:0001959.name: Polydipsia
HP:0001959.definition: Excessive thirst manifested by excessive fluid intake.

HP:0002180.name: Neurodegeneration
HP:0002180.definition: Progressive loss of neural cells and tissue.

HP:0002919.name: Ketonuria
HP:0002919.definition: High levels of ketone bodies (acetoacetic acid, beta-hydroxybutyric acid, and acetone) in the urine. Ketone bodies are insignificant in the blood and urine of normal individuals in the postprandial or overnight-fasted state.

HP:0003074.name: Hyperglycemia
HP:0003074.definition: An increased concentration of glucose in the blood.

HP:0007902.name: Vitreous hemorrhage
HP:0007902.definition: Bleeding within the vitreous compartment of the eye.

HP:0034062.name: Anti-insulin antibody positivity
HP:0034062.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against insulin.

HP:0000218.name: High palate
HP:0000218.definition: Height of the palate more than 2 SD above the mean (objective) or palatal height at the level of the first permanent molar more than twice the height of the teeth (subjective).

HP:0000348.name: High forehead
HP:0000348.definition: An abnormally increased height of the forehead.

HP:0000365.name: Hearing impairment
HP:0000365.definition: A decreased magnitude of the sensory perception of sound.

HP:0000410.name: Mixed hearing impairment
HP:0000410.definition: A type of hearing loss resulting from a combination of conductive hearing impairment and sensorineural hearing impairment.

HP:0000431.name: Wide nasal bridge
HP:0000431.definition: Increased breadth of the nasal bridge (and with it, the nasal root).

HP:0000478.name: Abnormality of the eye
HP:0000478.definition: Any abnormality of the eye, including location, spacing, and intraocular abnormalities.

HP:0000482.name: Microcornea
HP:0000482.definition: A congenital abnormality of the cornea in which the cornea and the anterior segment of the eye are smaller than normal. The horizontal diameter of the cornea does not reach 10 mm even in adulthood.
synonyms: Cornea of eye less than 10mm in diameter

HP:0000518.name: Cataract
HP:0000518.definition: A cataract is an opacity or clouding that develops in the crystalline lens of the eye or in its capsule.
synonyms: Clouding of the lens of the eye

HP:0000528.name: Anophthalmia
HP:0000528.definition: Absence of the globe or eyeball.

HP:0000567.name: Chorioretinal coloboma
HP:0000567.definition: Absence of a region of the retina, retinal pigment epithelium, and choroid.
synonyms: Birth defect that causes a hole in the innermost layer at the back of the eye

HP:0000568.name: Microphthalmia
HP:0000568.definition: A developmental anomaly characterized by abnormal smallness of one or both eyes.

HP:0000589.name: Coloboma
HP:0000589.definition: A developmental defect characterized by a cleft of some portion of the eye or ocular adnexa.

HP:0000646.name: Amblyopia
HP:0000646.definition: Reduced visual acuity that is uncorrectable by lenses in the absence of detectable anatomic defects in the eye or visual pathways.

HP:0000677.name: Oligodontia
HP:0000677.definition: The absence of six or more teeth from the normal series by a failure to develop.
synonyms: Failure of development of more than six teeth
Number of teeth decreased by more than six

HP:0000750.name: Delayed speech and language development
HP:0000750.definition: A degree of language development that is significantly below the norm for a child of a specified age.

HP:0001057.name: Aplasia cutis congenita
HP:0001057.definition: A developmental defect resulting in the congenital absence of skin in multiple or solitary non-inflammatory, well-demarcated, oval or circular ulcers with a diameter of about 1 to 2 cm. Aplasia cutis congenita most commonly occurs on the scalp, but may present in the face, trunk, or limbs.
synonyms: Absence of part of skin at birth

HP:0001132.name: Lens subluxation
HP:0001132.definition: Partial dislocation of the lens of the eye.

HP:0004484.name: Craniofacial asymmetry
HP:0004484.definition: Asymmetry of the bones of the skull and the face.

HP:0007269.name: Spinal muscular atrophy
HP:0007269.definition: Muscular weakness and atrophy related to loss of the motor neurons of the spinal cord and brainstem.

HP:0007678.name: Lacrimal duct stenosis
HP:0007678.definition: Narrowing of a tear duct (lacrimal duct).

HP:0007759.name: Opacification of the corneal stroma
HP:0007759.definition: Reduced transparency of the stroma of cornea.

HP:0100272.name: Branchial sinus
HP:0100272.definition: A congenital branchial sinus is a remnant of the embryonic branchial arches and their intervening clefts and pouches that has failed to regress completely. HP:0410030.name: Cleft lip
HP:0410030.definition: A gap in the lip or lips.

HP:6001302.name: Aphakia
HP:6001302.definition: Absence of the crystalline lens in the eye, which may be congenital or acquired (e.g., following surgical removal of the lens for cataracts or trauma).

HP:0000972.name: Palmoplantar hyperkeratosis
HP:0000972.definition: Abnormal thickening of the skin localized to the palm of the hand and the sole of the foot.
synonyms: Hyperkeratosis of the palms and soles

HP:0000999.name: Pyoderma
HP:0000999.definition: Any manifestation of a skin disease associated with the production of pus.

HP:0001166.name: Arachnodactyly
HP:0001166.definition: Abnormally long and slender fingers (spider fingers).

HP:0001249.name: Intellectual disability

HP:0002718.name: Recurrent bacterial infections
HP:0002718.definition: Increased susceptibility to bacterial infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of bacterial infection.

HP:0002719.name: Recurrent infections
HP:0002719.definition: Increased susceptibility to infections as manifested by repeated bouts of infection.

HP:0005406.name: Recurrent bacterial skin infections
HP:0005406.definition: Increased susceptibility to bacterial infections of the skin, as manifested by recurrent episodes of infectious dermatitis.

HP:0006323.name: Premature loss of primary teeth
HP:0006323.definition: Loss of the primary (also known as deciduous) teeth before the usual age.

HP:0006349.name: Agenesis of permanent teeth
HP:0006349.definition: A congenital defect characterized by the absence of one or more permanent teeth, including oligodontia, hypodontia, and adontia of the of permanent teeth.

HP:0010783.name: Erythema
HP:0010783.definition: Redness of the skin, caused by hyperemia of the capillaries in the lower layers of the skin.
synonyms: Redness of skin or mucous membrane

HP:0020083.name: Furuncle
HP:0020083.definition: An infection of a hair follicle that extends subcutaneously, forming an abscess.

HP:0025526.name: Psoriasiform lesion
HP:0025526.definition: A skin lesions that resembles the lesions observed in psoriasis, viz., an erythematous plaque covered by fine silvery scales. HP:0040189.name: Scaling skin
HP:0040189.definition: Refers to the loss of the outer layer of the epidermis in large, scale-like flakes.

HP:0100324.name: Scleroderma
HP:0100324.definition: A chronic autoimmune phenomenon characterized by fibrosis (or hardening) and vascular alterations of the skin.

HP:0100658.name: Cellulitis
HP:0100658.definition: A bacterial infection and inflammation of the skin und subcutaneous tissues.

HP:5210230.name: Recurrent boils
HP:5210230.definition: A recurrent infection of hair follicles producing furuncles (boils), with common causative organisms being Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus species. A recurrent boil can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in chronic granulomatous disease, hyper-IgE syndrom

HP:0000028.name: Cryptorchidism
HP:0000028.definition: Testis in inguinal canal. That is, absence of one or both testes from the scrotum owing to failure of the testis or testes to descend through the inguinal canal to the scrotum.

HP:0000100.name: Nephrotic syndrome
HP:0000100.definition: Nephrotic syndrome is a collection of findings resulting from glomerular dysfunction with an increase in glomerular capillary wall permeability associated with pronounced proteinuria. Nephrotic syndrome refers to the constellation of clinical findings that result from severe renal loss of protein, w

HP:0000256.name: Macrocephaly
HP:0000256.definition: Occipitofrontal (head) circumference greater than 97th centile compared to appropriate, age matched, sex-matched normal standards. Alternatively, a apparently increased size of the cranium.

HP:0000316.name: Hypertelorism
HP:0000316.definition: Interpupillary distance more than 2 SD above the mean (alternatively, the appearance of an increased interpupillary distance or widely spaced eyes).

HP:0000337.name: Broad forehead
HP:0000337.definition: Width of the forehead or distance between the frontotemporales is more than two standard deviations above the mean (objective); or apparently increased distance between the two sides of the forehead.

HP:0000358.name: Posteriorly rotated ears
HP:0000358.definition: A type of abnormal location of the ears in which the position of the ears is characterized by posterior rotation (the superior part of the ears is rotated towards the back of the head, and the inferior part of the ears towards the front).
synonyms: Ears rotated toward back of head

HP:0000360.name: Tinnitus
HP:0000360.definition: Tinnitus is an auditory perception that can be described as the experience of sound, in the ear or in the head, in the absence of external acoustic stimulation.

HP:0000369.name: Low-set ears
HP:0000369.definition: Upper insertion of the ear to the scalp below an imaginary horizontal line drawn between the inner canthi of the eye and extending posteriorly to the ear.

HP:0000407.name: Sensorineural hearing impairment
HP:0000407.definition: A type of hearing impairment in one or both ears related to an abnormal functionality of the cochlear nerve.

HP:0000475.name: Broad neck
HP:0000475.definition: Increased side-to-side width of the neck.

HP:0000494.name: Downslanted palpebral fissures
HP:0000494.definition: The palpebral fissure inclination is more than two standard deviations below the mean.

HP:0000508.name: Ptosis
HP:0000508.definition: The upper eyelid margin is positioned 3 mm or more lower than usual and covers the superior portion of the iris (objective); or, the upper lid margin obscures at least part of the pupil (subjective).

HP:0000766.name: Abnormal sternum morphology
HP:0000766.definition: An anomaly of the sternum, also known as the breastbone.

HP:0000767.name: Pectus excavatum
HP:0000767.definition: A defect of the chest wall characterized by a depression of the sternum, giving the chest ("pectus") a caved-in ("excavatum") appearance.

HP:0000819.name: Diabetes mellitus
HP:0000819.definition: A group of abnormalities characterized by hyperglycemia and glucose intolerance.

HP:0000823.name: Delayed puberty
HP:0000823.definition: Passing the age when puberty normally occurs with no physical or hormonal signs of the onset of puberty.

HP:0000953.name: Hyperpigmentation of the skin
HP:0000953.definition: A darkening of the skin related to an increase in melanin production and deposition.

HP:0000957.name: Cafe-au-lait spot
HP:0000957.definition: Cafe-au-lait spots are hyperpigmented lesions that can vary in color from light brown to dark brown with smooth borders and having a size of 1.5 cm or more in adults and 0.5 cm or more in children.

HP:0000962.name: Hyperkeratosis
HP:0000962.definition: Hyperkeratosis is a histopathological term defining a thickened stratum corneum and may be present in many different skin conditions, with many possible overlaps. HP:0000978.name: Bruising susceptibility
HP:0000978.definition: An ecchymosis (bruise) refers to the skin discoloration caused by the escape of blood into the tissues from ruptured blood vessels. HP:0001003.name: Multiple lentigines
HP:0001003.definition: Presence of an unusually high number of lentigines (singular: lentigo), which are flat, tan to brown oval spots.

HP:0001059.name: Pterygium
HP:0001059.definition: Pterygia are 'winglike' triangular membranes occurring in the neck, eyes, knees, elbows, ankles or digits.

HP:0001256.name: Mild intellectual disability
HP:0001256.definition: Mild intellectual disability (ID) is defined as a type of ID characterized by mildly sub-average adaptive functioning and intellectual functioning, with an intelligence quotient (IQ) the range of 50-69.

HP:0001263.name: Global developmental delay
HP:0001263.definition: A delay in the achievement of motor or mental milestones in the domains of development of a child, including motor skills, speech and language, cognitive skills, and social and emotional skills. This term should only be used to describe children younger than five years of age.

HP:0001270.name: Motor delay
HP:0001270.definition: A type of Developmental delay characterized by a delay in acquiring motor skills.
synonyms: Delay in development of motor milestones

HP:0001508.name: Failure to thrive
HP:0001508.definition: Failure to thrive (FTT) refers to a child whose physical growth is substantially below the norm.

HP:0001510.name: Growth delay
HP:0001510.definition: A deficiency or slowing down of growth pre- and postnatally.

HP:0001627.name: Abnormal heart morphology
HP:0001627.definition: Any structural anomaly of the heart.

HP:0001638.name: Cardiomyopathy
HP:0001638.definition: A myocardial disorder in which the heart muscle is structurally and functionally abnormal, in the absence of coronary artery disease, hypertension, valvular disease and congenital heart disease sufficient to cause the observed myocardial abnormality.

HP:0001892.name: Abnormal bleeding
HP:0001892.definition: An abnormal susceptibility to bleeding, often referred to as a bleeding diathesis. A bleeding diathesis may be related to vascular, platelet and coagulation defects.

HP:0001909.name: Leukemia
HP:0001909.definition: A cancer of the blood and bone marrow characterized by an abnormal proliferation of leukocytes.

HP:0002664.name: Neoplasm
HP:0002664.definition: An organ or organ-system abnormality that consists of uncontrolled autonomous cell-proliferation which can occur in any part of the body as a benign or malignant neoplasm (tumor).

HP:0004322.name: Short stature
HP:0004322.definition: A height below that which is expected according to age and gender norms. HP:0004482.name: Relative macrocephaly
HP:0004482.definition: A relatively mild degree of macrocephaly in which the head circumference is not above two standard deviations from the mean, but appears dysproportionately large when other factors such as body stature are taken into account.

HP:0007018.name: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder
HP:0007018.definition: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) manifests at age 2-3 years or by first grade at the latest. HP:0008527.name: Congenital sensorineural hearing impairment
HP:0008527.definition: A type of hearing impairment caused by an abnormal functionality of the cochlear nerve with congenital onset.

HP:0011968.name: Feeding difficulties
HP:0011968.definition: Impaired ability to eat related to problems gathering food and getting ready to suck, chew, or swallow it.

HP:0012209.name: Juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia
HP:0012209.definition: Juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia (JMML) is a lethal myeloproliferative disease of young childhood characterized clinically by overproduction of myelomonocytic cells and by the in vitro phenotype of hematopoietic progenitor hypersensitivity to granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor.

HP:0030148.name: Heart murmur
HP:0030148.definition: An extra or unusual sound heard during a heartbeat caused vibrations resulting from the flow of blood through the heart.

HP:0032152.name: Keratosis pilaris
HP:0032152.definition: An anomaly of the hair follicles of the skin that typically presents as small, rough, brown folliculocentric papules distributed over characteristic areas of the skin, particularly the outer-upper arms and thighs.

HP:0033609.name: Solid pulmonary nodule
HP:0033609.definition: A type of pulmonary nodule whose density obscures the underlying parenchyma and thus has a "solid" appearance.

HP:0001382.name: Joint hypermobility
HP:0001382.definition: The capability that a joint (or a group of joints) has to move, passively and/or actively, beyond normal limits along physiological axes.

HP:0002515.definition: Weakness of the hip girdle and upper thigh muscles, for instance in myopathies, leads to an instability of the pelvis on standing and walking. HP:0002758.definition: Degeneration (wear and tear) of articular cartilage, i.e., of the joint surface. Joint degeneration may be accompanied by osteophytes (bone overgrowth), narrowing of the joint space, regions of sclerosis at the joint surface, or joint deformity.

HP:0003026.name: Short long bone
HP:0003026.definition: One or more abnormally short long bone.

HP:0003498.name: Disproportionate short stature
HP:0003498.definition: A kind of short stature in which different regions of the body are shortened to differing extents.

HP:0009381.name: Short finger
HP:0009381.definition: Abnormally short finger associated with developmental hypoplasia.

HP:0009826.name: Limb undergrowth
HP:0009826.definition: Limb shortening because of underdevelopment of one or more bones of the extremities.

HP:0000707.name: Abnormality of the nervous system
HP:0000707.definition: An abnormality of the nervous system.

HP:0000737.name: Irritability
HP:0000737.definition: An emotional state characterized by negative feelings of heightened frustration, annoyance, or feeling upset, often triggered by internal factors (e.g., fatigue, hunger, unfulfilled desires) or external factors (e.g., social or environmental challenges). HP:0000952.name: Jaundice
HP:0000952.definition: Yellow pigmentation of the skin due to bilirubin, which in turn is the result of increased bilirubin concentration in the bloodstream.

HP:0000969.name: Edema
HP:0000969.definition: An abnormal accumulation of fluid beneath the skin, or in one or more cavities of the body.

HP:0001250.name: Seizure
HP:0001250.definition: A seizure is an intermittent abnormality of nervous system physiology characterized by a transient occurrence of signs and/or symptoms due to abnormal excessive or synchronous neuronal activity in the brain.

HP:0001251.name: Ataxia
HP:0001251.definition: Ataxia refers to impaired coordination of voluntary muscle movement. Cerebellar ataxia refers to ataxia due to dysfunction of the cerebellum. HP:0100960.definition: Abnormal difference in size between the left and right lateral cerebral ventricles.

HP:0000218.definition: Height of the palate more than 2 SD above the mean (objective) or palatal height at the level of the first permanent molar more than twice the height of the teeth (subjective).

HP:0000232.definition: An abnormal configuration of the lower lip such that it is turned outward i.e., everted, with the Inner aspect of the lower lip vermilion (normally opposing the teeth) being visible in a frontal view.

HP:0000243.definition: Wedge-shaped, or triangular head, with the apex of the triangle at the midline of the forehead and the base of the triangle at the occiput.

HP:0000325.definition: Facial contour, as viewed from the front, triangular in shape, with breadth at the temples and tapering to a narrow chin.

HP:0000377.definition: An abnormality of the pinna, which is also referred to as the auricle or external ear.

HP:0000407.definition: A type of hearing impairment in one or both ears related to an abnormal functionality of the cochlear nerve.

HP:0000414.definition: Increased volume and globular shape of the anteroinferior aspect of the nose.

HP:0000457.name: Depressed nasal ridge
HP:0000457.definition: Lack of prominence of the nose resulting from a posteriorly-placed nasal ridge.

HP:0000750.definition: A degree of language development that is significantly below the norm for a child of a specified age.

HP:0000889.name: Abnormal clavicle morphology
HP:0000889.definition: Any abnormality of the clavicles (collar bones).

HP:0000960.name: Sacral dimple
HP:0000960.definition: A cutaneous indentation resulting from tethering of the skin to underlying structures (bone) of the intergluteal cleft.

HP:0001166.name: Arachnodactyly
HP:0001166.definition: Abnormally long and slender fingers (spider fingers).

HP:0001195.name: Single umbilical artery
HP:0001195.definition: Single umbilical artery (SUA) is the absence of one of the two umbilical arteries surrounding the fetal bladder and in the fetal umbilical cord.

HP:0001328.definition: Impairment of certain skills such as reading or writing, coordination, self-control, or attention that interfere with the ability to learn. The impairment is not related to a global deficiency of intelligence.

HP:0001371.definition: A flexion contracture is a bent (flexed) joint that cannot be straightened actively or passively. It is thus a chronic loss of joint motion due to structural changes in muscle, tendons, ligaments, or skin that prevents normal movement of joints.
synonyms: Flexed joint that cannot be straightened

HP:0001382.name: Joint hypermobility
HP:0001382.definition: The capability that a joint (or a group of joints) has to move, passively and/or actively, beyond normal limits along physiological axes.

HP:0001631.name: Atrial septal defect
HP:0001631.definition: Atrial septal defect (ASD) is a congenital abnormality of the interatrial septum that enables blood flow between the left and right atria via the interatrial septum.
synonyms: An opening in the wall separating the top two chambers of the heart

HP:0001760.name: Abnormal foot morphology
HP:0001760.definition: An abnormality of the skeleton of foot.

HP:0001762.definition: Talipes equinovarus (also called clubfoot) typically has four main components: inversion and adduction of the forefoot; inversion of the heel and hindfoot; equinus (limitation of extension) of the ankle and subtalar joint; and internal rotation of the leg.

HP:0001763.name: Pes planus
HP:0001763.definition: A foot where the longitudinal arch of the foot is in contact with the ground or floor when the individual is standing; or, in a patient lying supine, a foot where the arch is in contact with the surface of a flat board pressed against the sole of the foot by the examiner with a pressure similar to t

HP:0001792.name: Small nail
HP:0001792.definition: A nail that is diminished in length and width, i.e., underdeveloped nail.

HP:0002650.name: Scoliosis
HP:0002650.definition: The presence of an abnormal lateral curvature of the spine.
synonyms: Cobb angle greater than ten degrees

HP:0002751.name: Kyphoscoliosis
HP:0002751.definition: An abnormal curvature of the spine in both a coronal (lateral) and sagittal (back-to-front) plane.

HP:0002761.definition: Joint hypermobility (ability of a joint to move beyond its normal range of motion) affecting many or all joints of the body. In individuals with Joint hypermobility at multiple sites (usually five or more), the term generalized joint hypermobility is preferred.

HP:0002857.definition: The legs angle inward, such that the knees are close together and the ankles far apart.

HP:0002901.name: Hypocalcemia
HP:0002901.definition: The concentration of calcium in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

HP:0002999.definition: The kneecap normally is located within the groove termed trochlea on the distal femur and can slide up and down in it. Patellar dislocation occurs if the patella fully dislocates out of the groove.

HP:0003083.name: Dislocated radial head
HP:0003083.definition: A dislocation of the head of the radius from its socket in the elbow joint.

HP:0004411.name: Deviated nasal septum
HP:0004411.definition: Positioning of the nasal septum to the right or left in contrast to the normal midline position of the nasal septum.

HP:0004691.name: 2-3 toe syndactyly
HP:0004691.definition: Syndactyly with fusion of toes two and three.

HP:0005280.name: Depressed nasal bridge
HP:0005280.definition: Posterior positioning of the nasal root in relation to the overall facial profile for age.

HP:0009882.name: Short distal phalanx of finger
HP:0009882.definition: Short distance from the end of the finger to the most distal interphalangeal crease or the distal interphalangeal joint flexion point. That is, hypoplasia of one or more of the distal phalanx of finger.

HP:0010499.name: Patellar subluxation
HP:0010499.definition: The kneecap normally is located within the groove termed trochlea on the distal femur and can slide up and down in it. Patellar subluxation refers to an unstable kneecap that does not slide centrally within its groove, i.e., a partial dislocation of the patella.

HP:0010864.definition: Severe intellectual disability (ID) is defined as a type of ID characterized by severely sub-average adaptive functioning and intellectual functioning, with an intelligence quotient (IQ) the range of 20-34.

HP:0010946.name: Dilatation of the renal pelvis
HP:0010946.definition: The presence of dilatation of the renal pelvis.

HP:0012385.name: Camptodactyly
HP:0012385.definition: The distal interphalangeal joint and/or the proximal interphalangeal joint of the fingers or toes cannot be extended to 180 degrees by either active or passive extension.

HP:0025259.name: Stiff elbow
HP:0025259.definition: A sensation of tightness in the elbow joint when attempting to move it, especially after a period of inactivity.

HP:0030084.name: Clinodactyly
HP:0030084.definition: An angulation of a digit at an interphalangeal joint in the plane of the palm (finger) or sole (toe).

HP:0030799.name: Scaphocephaly
HP:0030799.definition: Scaphocephaly is a subtype of dolichocephaly where the anterior and posterior aspects of the cranial vault are pointed (boat-shaped). Scaphocephaly is caused by a precocious fusion of sagittal suture without other associated synostosis.

HP:0034392.name: Joint contracture
HP:0034392.definition: A limitation in the passive range of motion of a joint resulting from loss of elasticity in the periarticular tissues owing to structural changes of non-bony tissues, such as muscles, tendons, ligaments, joint capsules or skin. HP:0011675.definition: Any cardiac rhythm other than the normal sinus rhythm. Such a rhythm may be either of sinus or ectopic origin and either regular or irregular. An arrhythmia may be due to a disturbance in impulse formation or conduction or both.

HP:0012520.name: Dilation of Virchow-Robin spaces
HP:0012520.definition: Increased dimensions of the Virchow-Robin spaces (also known as perivascular spaces), which surround the walls of vessels as they course from the subarachnoid space through the brain parenchyma. HP:0012759.name: Neurodevelopmental abnormality
HP:0012759.definition: A deviation from normal of the neurological development of a child, which may include any or all of the aspects of the development of personal, social, gross or fine motor, and cognitive abilities.

HP:0025161.name: Frequent temper tantrums
HP:0025161.definition: Temper tantrums that occur more frequently compared to the temper tantrums that are a part of the normal developmental process.

HP:0030746.name: Intraventricular hemorrhage
HP:0030746.definition: Bleeding into the ventricles of the brain.

HP:0033044.name: Motor regression
HP:0033044.definition: Loss of previously achieved motor skills, as manifested by loss of developmental motor milestones.

HP:0000737.definition: An emotional state characterized by negative feelings of heightened frustration, annoyance, or feeling upset, often triggered by internal factors (e.g., fatigue, hunger, unfulfilled desires) or external factors (e.g., social or environmental challenges). HP:0000822.name: Hypertension
HP:0000822.definition: The presence of chronic increased pressure in the systemic arterial system.

HP:0000962.name: Hyperkeratosis
HP:0000962.definition: Hyperkeratosis is a histopathological term defining a thickened stratum corneum and may be present in many different skin conditions, with many possible overlaps. HP:0000975.name: Hyperhidrosis
HP:0000975.definition: Abnormal excessive perspiration (sweating) despite the lack of appropriate stimuli like hot and humid weather.

HP:0000989.name: Pruritus
HP:0000989.definition: Pruritus is an itch or a sensation that makes a person want to scratch. This term refers to an abnormally increased disposition to experience pruritus.

HP:0000995.name: Melanocytic nevus
HP:0000995.definition: A oval and round, colored (usually medium-to dark brown, reddish brown, or flesh colored) lesion. Typically, a melanocytic nevus is less than 6 mm in diameter, but may be much smaller or larger.

HP:0001028.name: Hemangioma
HP:0001028.definition: A hemangioma is a benign tumor characterized by blood-filled spaces lined by benign endothelial cells. A hemangioma characterized by large endothelial spaces (caverns) is called a cavernous hemangioma (in contrast to a hemangioma with small endothelial spaces, which is called capillary hemangioma).

HP:0001249.name: Intellectual disability

HP:0001252.name: Hypotonia

HP:0001263.name: Global developmental delay
HP:0001263.definition: A delay in the achievement of motor or mental milestones in the domains of development of a child, including motor skills, speech and language, cognitive skills, and social and emotional skills. This term should only be used to describe children younger than five years of age.

HP:0001508.name: Failure to thrive
HP:0001508.definition: Failure to thrive (FTT) refers to a child whose physical growth is substantially below the norm.

HP:0001627.name: Abnormal heart morphology
HP:0001627.definition: Any structural anomaly of the heart.

HP:0001629.name: Ventricular septal defect
HP:0001629.definition: A hole between the two bottom chambers (ventricles) of the heart. The defect is centered around the most superior aspect of the ventricular septum.
synonyms: Hole in heart wall separating two lower heart chambers

HP:0001635.name: Congestive heart failure
HP:0001635.definition: The presence of an abnormality of cardiac function that is responsible for the failure of the heart to pump blood at a rate that is commensurate with the needs of the tissues or a state in which abnormally elevated filling pressures are required for the heart to do so. Heart failure is frequently re

HP:0001639.name: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
HP:0001639.definition: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is defined by the presence of increased ventricular wall thickness or mass in the absence of loading conditions (hypertension, valve disease) sufficient to cause the observed abnormality.

HP:0001671.name: Abnormal cardiac septum morphology
HP:0001671.definition: An anomaly of the intra-atrial or intraventricular septum.

HP:0001945.name: Fever
HP:0001945.definition: Body temperature elevated above the normal range.

HP:0002007.name: Frontal bossing
HP:0002007.definition: Bilateral bulging of the lateral frontal bone prominences with relative sparing of the midline.

HP:0002046.name: Heat intolerance
HP:0002046.definition: The inability to maintain a comfortable body temperature in warm or hot weather.

HP:0002835.name: Aspiration
HP:0002835.definition: Inspiration of a foreign object into the airway.

HP:0002901.name: Hypocalcemia
HP:0002901.definition: The concentration of calcium in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

HP:0004482.name: Relative macrocephaly
HP:0004482.definition: A relatively mild degree of macrocephaly in which the head circumference is not above two standard deviations from the mean, but appears dysproportionately large when other factors such as body stature are taken into account.

HP:0004484.name: Craniofacial asymmetry
HP:0004484.definition: Asymmetry of the bones of the skull and the face.

HP:0004523.name: Long eyebrows
HP:0004523.definition: Increased length of the hairs of the eyebrows.

HP:0006610.name: Wide intermamillary distance
HP:0006610.definition: A larger than usual distance between the left and right nipple.

HP:0008064.name: Ichthyosis
HP:0008064.definition: An abnormality of the skin characterized the presence of excessive amounts of dry surface scales on the skin resulting from an abnormality of keratinization.

HP:0009890.name: High anterior hairline
HP:0009890.definition: Distance between the hairline (trichion) and the glabella (the most prominent point on the frontal bone above the root of the nose), in the midline, more than two SD above the mean. Alternatively, an apparently increased distance between the hairline and the glabella.

HP:0011344.name: Severe global developmental delay
HP:0011344.definition: A severe delay in the achievement of motor or mental milestones in the domains of development of a child.

HP:0011675.name: Arrhythmia
HP:0011675.definition: Any cardiac rhythm other than the normal sinus rhythm. Such a rhythm may be either of sinus or ectopic origin and either regular or irregular. An arrhythmia may be due to a disturbance in impulse formation or conduction or both.

HP:0011968.name: Feeding difficulties
HP:0011968.definition: Impaired ability to eat related to problems gathering food and getting ready to suck, chew, or swallow it.

HP:0025084.name: Folliculitis
HP:0025084.definition: Inflammatory cells within the wall and ostia of the hair follicle, creating a follicular-based pustule.

HP:0032152.name: Keratosis pilaris
HP:0032152.definition: An anomaly of the hair follicles of the skin that typically presents as small, rough, brown folliculocentric papules distributed over characteristic areas of the skin, particularly the outer-upper arms and thighs.

HP:0032252.name: Granuloma
HP:0032252.definition: A compact, organized collection of mature mononuclear phagocytes, which may be but is not necessarily accompanied by accessory features such as necrosis.

HP:0045059.name: Hyperkeratotic papule
HP:0045059.definition: A circumscribed, solid elevation of skin with no visible fluid, varying in size from a pinhead to less than 10mm in diameter at the widest point that is composed of localized hyperkeratosis (the latter may be demonstrated histopathologically).

HP:0200034.name: Papule
HP:0200034.definition: A circumscribed, solid elevation of skin with no visible fluid, varying in size from a pinhead to less than 10mm in diameter at the widest point.

HP:6001166.name: Spongiosis

HP:0000488.name: Retinopathy
HP:0000488.definition: Any noninflammatory disease of the retina. This nonspecific term is retained here because of its wide use in the literature, but if possible new annotations should indicate the precise type of retinal abnormality.

HP:0000505.name: Visual impairment

HP:0000510.definition: An inherited retinal disease subtype in which the rod photoreceptors appear to be more severely affected than the cone photoreceptors. HP:0000518.name: Cataract
HP:0000518.definition: A cataract is an opacity or clouding that develops in the crystalline lens of the eye or in its capsule.
synonyms: Clouding of the lens of the eye

HP:0000543.name: Optic disc pallor
HP:0000543.definition: A pale yellow discoloration of the optic disc (the area of the optic nerve head in the retina). The optic disc normally has a pinkish hue with a central yellowish depression.

HP:0000551.name: Color vision defect
HP:0000551.definition: An anomaly in the ability to discriminate between or recognize colors.

HP:0000556.name: Retinal dystrophy
HP:0000556.definition: Retinal dystrophy is an abnormality of the retina associated with a hereditary process. Retinal dystrophies are defined by their predominantly monogenic inheritance and they are frequently associated with loss or dysfunction of photoreceptor cells as a primary or secondary event.
synonyms: Breakdown of light-sensitive cells in back of eye

HP:0000572.name: Visual loss
HP:0000572.definition: Loss of visual acuity (implying that vision was better at a certain time point in life). Otherwise the term reduced visual acuity should be used (or a subclass of that).

HP:0000575.name: Scotoma
HP:0000575.definition: A regional and pathological increase of the light detection threshold in any region of the visual field surrounded by a field of normal or relatively well-preserved vision.

HP:0000618.name: Blindness
HP:0000618.definition: Blindness is the condition of lacking visual perception defined as a profound reduction in visual perception. HP:0000639.name: Nystagmus
HP:0000639.definition: Rhythmic, involuntary oscillations of one or both eyes related to abnormality in fixation, conjugate gaze, or vestibular mechanisms.

HP:0000648.name: Optic atrophy
HP:0000648.definition: Atrophy of the optic nerve. Optic atrophy results from the death of the retinal ganglion cell axons that comprise the optic nerve and manifesting as a pale optic nerve on fundoscopy.

HP:0000662.name: Nyctalopia
HP:0000662.definition: Inability to see well at night or in poor light.

HP:0000666.name: Horizontal nystagmus
HP:0000666.definition: Nystagmus consisting of horizontal to-and-fro eye movements.

HP:0000822.name: Hypertension
HP:0000822.definition: The presence of chronic increased pressure in the systemic arterial system.

HP:0001000.name: Abnormal skin pigmentation
HP:0001000.definition: An abnormality of the pigmentation of the skin.

HP:0001105.name: Retinal atrophy
HP:0001105.definition: A nonspecific term denoting wasting, especially as a result of degeneration, of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and neurosensory retinal cells.

HP:0001141.name: Severely reduced visual acuity
HP:0001141.definition: Severe reduction of the ability to see. On the 6m visual acuity scale, severe reduction is defined as less than 6/60 but at least 3/60. HP:0001583.name: Rotary nystagmus
HP:0001583.definition: A form of nystagmus in which the eyeball makes rotary motions around the axis.

HP:0002172.name: Postural instability
HP:0002172.definition: A tendency to fall or the inability to keep oneself from falling; imbalance. HP:0004322.definition: A height below that which is expected according to age and gender norms. HP:0007401.name: Macular atrophy
HP:0007401.definition: A nonspecific term denoting wasting, especially as a result of degeneration, of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and neurosensory retinal cells in the macula.

HP:0007754.name: Macular dystrophy
HP:0007754.definition: Macular dystrophy is a nonspecific term for retinal degeneration, generally confined to the macula, usually presumed of genetic origin.

HP:0007814.name: Retinal pigment epithelial mottling
HP:0007814.definition: Mottling (spots or blotches of different shades) of the retinal pigment epithelium, i.e., localized or generalized fundus pigment granularity associated with processes at the level of the retinal pigment epithelium.
synonyms: Focal hypopigmentation of the retinal pigment epithelium

HP:0008043.name: Focal retinal arteriolar constriction
HP:0008043.definition: Focal decreased retinal arteriolar diameters, which may decrease blood flow and slow oxygen delivery to regions of the retina.

HP:0011516.name: Achromatopsia
HP:0011516.definition: A condition where the retina contains no functional cone cells, so that in addition to the absence of color discrimination, vision in lights of normal intensity is difficult.

HP:0025010.name: Foveal atrophy
HP:0025010.definition: A nonspecific term denoting wasting, especially as a result of degeneration, of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and neurosensory retinal cells in the fovea.

HP:0030637.name: Congenital stationary cone dysfunction
HP:0030637.definition: Retinal phenotype characterized by cone photoreceptor dysfunction and preserved rod system. The abnormality is typically stationary or very slowly progressive and findings may include reduced central vision, color vision abnormalities, nystagmus and photophobia.

HP:0500041.name: Myopic astigmatism
HP:0500041.definition: A condition where one or both of the two principal meridians focus in the front of the retina when the eye is at rest.

HP:0001338.definition: A partial failure of the development of the corpus callosum.

HP:0001360.name: Holoprosencephaly
HP:0001360.definition: Holoprosencephaly is a structural anomaly of the brain in which the developing forebrain fails to divide into two separate hemispheres and ventricles.

HP:0001627.name: Abnormal heart morphology
HP:0001627.definition: Any structural anomaly of the heart.

HP:0001999.name: Abnormal facial shape
HP:0001999.definition: An abnormal morphology (form) of the face or its components.

HP:0002119.name: Ventriculomegaly
HP:0002119.definition: An increase in size of the ventricular system of the brain.

HP:0002198.name: Dilated fourth ventricle
HP:0002198.definition: An abnormal dilatation of the fourth cerebral ventricle.

HP:0002389.definition: If the two laminae of the septum pellucidum are not fused then a fluid-filled space or cavum is present. HP:0002664.name: Neoplasm
HP:0002664.definition: An organ or organ-system abnormality that consists of uncontrolled autonomous cell-proliferation which can occur in any part of the body as a benign or malignant neoplasm (tumor).

HP:0004484.name: Craniofacial asymmetry
HP:0004484.definition: Asymmetry of the bones of the skull and the face.

HP:0007359.name: Focal-onset seizure
HP:0007359.definition: A focal-onset seizure is a type of seizure originating within networks limited to one hemisphere. They may be discretely localized or more widely distributed, and may originate in subcortical structures.

HP:0010880.name: Increased nuchal translucency
HP:0010880.definition: Nuchal translucency is the sonographic appearance of subcutaneous accumulation of liquid in the back of the fetal neck in the first trimester of pregnancy (11-14 gestational weeks of pregnancy).

HP:0012443.name: Abnormal brain morphology
HP:0012443.definition: A structural abnormality of the brain, which has as its parts the forebrain, midbrain, and hindbrain.

HP:0012759.name: Neurodevelopmental abnormality
HP:0012759.definition: A deviation from normal of the neurological development of a child, which may include any or all of the aspects of the development of personal, social, gross or fine motor, and cognitive abilities.

HP:0033140.definition: The presence of an upwardly displaced normal cerebellar vermis, normal appearance of the fastigium, tentorium and size of the cisterna magna.

HP:0034057.name: Fetal anomaly
HP:0034057.definition: Structural or functional abnormalities of the fetus. HP:0100615.name: Ovarian neoplasm
HP:0100615.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the ovary.

HP:0000316.definition: Interpupillary distance more than 2 SD above the mean (alternatively, the appearance of an increased interpupillary distance or widely spaced eyes).

HP:0000321.name: Square face
HP:0000321.definition: Facial contours, as viewed from the front, show a broad upper face/cranium and lower face/mandible, creating a square appearance.

HP:0000707.name: Abnormality of the nervous system
HP:0000707.definition: An abnormality of the nervous system.

HP:0000717.name: Autism
HP:0000717.definition: Autism is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by impaired social interaction and communication, and by restricted and repetitive behavior. Autism begins in childhood. HP:0001268.definition: Loss of previously present mental abilities, generally in adults.

HP:0001270.name: Motor delay
HP:0001270.definition: A type of Developmental delay characterized by a delay in acquiring motor skills.

HP:0001347.name: Hyperreflexia
HP:0001347.definition: Hyperreflexia is the presence of hyperactive stretch reflexes of the muscles.

HP:0002061.name: Lower limb spasticity
HP:0002061.definition: Spasticity (velocity-dependent increase in tonic stretch reflexes with increased muscle tone and hyperexcitable tendon reflexes) in the muscles of the lower limbs, hips, and pelvis.

HP:0002169.name: Clonus
HP:0002169.definition: A series of rhythmic and involuntary muscle contractions (at a frequency of about 5 to 7 Hz) that occur in response to an abruptly applied and sustained stretch.
synonyms: Involuntary rhythmic muscular contractions and relaxations

HP:0002191.name: Progressive spasticity

HP:0002263.definition: More pronounced paramedian peaks and median notch of the Cupid's bow.

HP:0002329.name: Drowsiness
HP:0002329.definition: Abnormal feeling of sleepiness or difficulty staying awake.

HP:0002353.name: EEG abnormality
HP:0002353.definition: Abnormality observed by electroencephalogram (EEG), which is used to record of the brain's spontaneous electrical activity from multiple electrodes placed on the scalp.

HP:0002579.name: Gastrointestinal dysmotility
HP:0002579.definition: Abnormal intestinal contractions, such as spasms and intestinal paralysis, related to the loss of the ability of the gut to coordinate muscular activity because of endogenous or exogenous causes.

HP:0003487.name: Babinski sign
HP:0003487.definition: Upturning of the big toe (and sometimes fanning of the other toes) in response to stimulation of the sole of the foot. If the Babinski sign is present it can indicate damage to the corticospinal tract.

HP:0007256.name: Abnormal pyramidal sign
HP:0007256.definition: Functional neurological abnormalities related to dysfunction of the pyramidal tract.

HP:0009830.name: Peripheral neuropathy
HP:0009830.definition: Peripheral neuropathy is a general term for any disorder of the peripheral nervous system. The main clinical features used to classify peripheral neuropathy are distribution, type (mainly demyelinating versus mainly axonal), duration, and course.

HP:0012103.name: Abnormality of the mitochondrion
HP:0012103.definition: An anomaly of the mitochondrion, the membranous cytoplasmic organelle the interior of which is subdivided by cristae. The mitochondrion is a self replicating organelle that is the site of tissue respiration.

HP:0025406.name: Asthenia
HP:0025406.definition: A state characterized by a feeling of weakness and loss of strength leading to a generalized weakness of the body.

HP:0100021.name: Cerebral palsy
HP:0100021.definition: Cerebral palsy describes a group of permanent disorders of the development of movement and posture, causing activity limitation, that are attributed to nonprogressive disturbances that occurred in the developing fetal or infant brain. HP:0100022.name: Abnormality of movement
HP:0100022.definition: An abnormality of movement with a neurological basis characterized by changes in coordination and speed of voluntary movements.

HP:0000388.name: Otitis media
HP:0000388.definition: Inflammation or infection of the middle ear.

HP:0000421.name: Epistaxis
HP:0000421.definition: Epistaxis, or nosebleed, refers to a hemorrhage localized in the nose.

HP:0001873.name: Thrombocytopenia
HP:0001873.definition: A reduction in the number of circulating thrombocytes.

HP:0001875.name: Decreased total neutrophil count
HP:0001875.definition: Abnormal decrease of absolute number of neutrophils in the blood, per microlitre, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.

HP:0001888.name: Decreased total lymphocyte count
HP:0001888.definition: A reduced number of lymphocytes in the blood.

HP:0002090.name: Pneumonia
HP:0002090.definition: Inflammation of any part of the lung parenchyma.

HP:0002110.name: Bronchiectasis
HP:0002110.definition: Persistent abnormal dilatation of the bronchi owing to localized and irreversible destruction and widening of the large airways.
synonyms: Permanent enlargement of the airways of the lungs

HP:0002205.name: Recurrent respiratory infections
HP:0002205.definition: An increased susceptibility to respiratory infections as manifested by a history of recurrent respiratory infections.

HP:0002242.name: Abnormal intestine morphology
HP:0002242.definition: An abnormality of the intestine. The closely related term enteropathy is used to refer to any disease of the intestine.

HP:0002719.name: Recurrent infections
HP:0002719.definition: Increased susceptibility to infections as manifested by repeated bouts of infection.

HP:0002721.name: Immunodeficiency
HP:0002721.definition: Failure of the immune system to protect the body adequately from infection, due to the absence or insufficiency of some component process or substance.

HP:0002788.name: Recurrent upper respiratory tract infections
HP:0002788.definition: An increased susceptibility to upper respiratory tract infections as manifested by a history of recurrent upper respiratory tract infections (running ears - otitis, sinusitis, pharyngitis, tonsillitis).

HP:0002958.name: Immune dysregulation
HP:0002958.definition: Altered immune function characterized by lymphoid proliferation, immune activation, and excessive autoreactivity often leading to autoimmune/inflammatory complications.

HP:0002960.name: Autoimmunity
HP:0002960.definition: The occurrence of an immune reaction against the organism's own cells or tissues.

HP:0003765.name: Psoriasiform dermatitis
HP:0003765.definition: A skin abnormality characterized by redness and irritation, with thick, red skin that displays flaky, silver-white patches (scales).

HP:0004313.name: Decreased circulating immunoglobulin concentration
HP:0004313.definition: An abnormally decreased level of immunoglobulin in blood.

HP:0004432.name: Agammaglobulinemia
HP:0004432.definition: A lasting absence of total IgG and total IgA and total IgM in the blood circulation, whereby at most trace quantities can be measured.

HP:0009830.name: Peripheral neuropathy
HP:0009830.definition: Peripheral neuropathy is a general term for any disorder of the peripheral nervous system. The main clinical features used to classify peripheral neuropathy are distribution, type (mainly demyelinating versus mainly axonal), duration, and course.

HP:0011947.name: Respiratory tract infection
HP:0011947.definition: An infection of the upper or lower respiratory tract.

HP:0030731.name: Carcinoma
HP:0030731.definition: A malignant tumor arising from epithelial cells. HP:0031160.name: Myelokathexis
HP:0031160.definition: Impaired egress of mature neutrophils from bone marrow causing neutropenia.

HP:0032154.name: Aphthous ulcer
HP:0032154.definition: Oral aphthous ulcers typically present as painful, sharply circumscribed fibrin-covered mucosal defects with a hyperemic border.

HP:0032301.name: Genital warts
HP:0032301.definition: Warts affecting the skin in the genital area (penile shaft, scrotum, vagina, or labia majora). Warts can be small, beginning as a pinhead-size swelling that may become larger and take on a pedunculated appearance. Warts can spread and coalesce into large masses in the genital or anal area. HP:0200043.name: Verrucae
HP:0200043.definition: Warts, benign growths on the skin or mucous membranes that cause cosmetic problems as well as pain and discomfort. Warts most often occur on the hands, feet, and genital areas.

HP:0410252.name: Persistently decreased total neutrophil count
HP:0410252.definition: Abnormal decrease of the absolute number of neutrophils in the blood, per microlitre, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group, which persists for 3 or more months.

HP:5210305.name: Recurrent warts
HP:5210305.definition: Increased susceptibility to human papillomavirus (HPV), manifested by recurrent episodes of warts.

HP:0000202.name: Orofacial cleft
HP:0000202.definition: The presence of a cleft (gap, opening, or groove) in the oral cavity, including cleft of the upper lip and/or cleft of the palate. HP:0000924.name: Abnormality of the skeletal system
HP:0000924.definition: An abnormality of the skeletal system.

HP:0000968.name: Ectodermal dysplasia
HP:0000968.definition: Ectodermal dysplasia is a group of conditions in which there is abnormal development of the skin, hair, nails, teeth, or sweat glands.

HP:0001000.name: Abnormal skin pigmentation
HP:0001000.definition: An abnormality of the pigmentation of the skin.

HP:0001159.name: Syndactyly
HP:0001159.definition: Webbing or fusion of the fingers or toes, involving soft parts only or including bone structure. Bony fusions are referred to as "bony" syndactyly if the fusion occurs in a radio-ulnar axis. Fusions of bones of the fingers or toes in a proximo-distal axis are referred to as "symphalangism".

HP:0001171.name: Split hand
HP:0001171.definition: A condition in which middle parts of the hand (fingers and metacarpals) are missing giving a cleft appearance. The severity is very variable ranging from slightly hypoplastic middle fingers over absent middle fingers as far as oligo- or monodactyl hands.

HP:0001252.name: Hypotonia
HP:0001252.definition: Hypotonia is an abnormally low muscle tone (the amount of tension or resistance to movement in a muscle). Even when relaxed, muscles have a continuous and passive partial contraction which provides some resistance to passive stretching. Hypotonia thus manifests as diminished resistance to passive st

HP:0001770.name: Toe syndactyly
HP:0001770.definition: Webbing or fusion of the toes, involving soft parts only or including bone structure. Bony fusions are referred to as "bony" Syndactyly if the fusion occurs in a radio-ulnar axis. Fusions of bones of the toes in a proximo-distal axis are referred to as "Symphalangism".

HP:0001839.name: Split foot
HP:0001839.definition: A condition in which middle parts of the foot (toes and metatarsals) are missing giving a cleft appearance. The severity is very variable ranging from slightly hypoplastic 3rd toe over absent 2nd or 3rd toes as far as oligo- or monodactyl feet.

HP:0002664.name: Neoplasm
HP:0002664.definition: An organ or organ-system abnormality that consists of uncontrolled autonomous cell-proliferation which can occur in any part of the body as a benign or malignant neoplasm (tumor).

HP:0002813.name: Abnormal limb bone morphology
HP:0002813.definition: Any abnormality of bones of the arms or legs.

HP:0009380.name: Finger aplasia
HP:0009380.definition: A developmental defect resulting in the presence of fewer than the normal number of fingers (i.e., aplasia of one or more fingers).

HP:0009755.name: Ankyloblepharon
HP:0009755.definition: Partial fusion of the upper and lower eyelid margins by single or multiple bands of tissue.

HP:0010442.name: Polydactyly
HP:0010442.definition: A congenital anomaly characterized by the presence of supernumerary fingers or toes.
synonyms: More than five fingers or toes on hands or feet

HP:0012385.name: Camptodactyly
HP:0012385.definition: The distal interphalangeal joint and/or the proximal interphalangeal joint of the fingers or toes cannot be extended to 180 degrees by either active or passive extension.
synonyms: Permanent flexion of the finger or toe

HP:0030084.name: Clinodactyly
HP:0030084.definition: An angulation of a digit at an interphalangeal joint in the plane of the palm (finger) or sole (toe).

HP:0034057.name: Fetal anomaly
HP:0034057.definition: Structural or functional abnormalities of the fetus. Note that this section comprises terms that describe abnormalities that are specific to the fetus or differ from the corresponding general terms. A term from anywhere in the Human Phenotype Ontology can be applied to a fetus if appropriate.

HP:0100257.name: Ectrodactyly
HP:0100257.definition: A condition in which middle parts of the hands and/or feet (digits and meta-carpals and -tarsals) are missing giving a cleft appearance. HP:0000248.definition: An abnormality of skull shape characterized by a decreased anterior-posterior diameter. That is, a cephalic index greater than 81%. Alternatively, an apparently shortened anteroposterior dimension (length) of the head compared to width.

HP:0000252.name: Microcephaly
HP:0000252.definition: Head circumference below 2 standard deviations below the mean for age and gender.

HP:0000316.name: Hypertelorism
HP:0000316.definition: Interpupillary distance more than 2 SD above the mean (alternatively, the appearance of an increased interpupillary distance or widely spaced eyes).

HP:0000343.name: Long philtrum
HP:0000343.definition: Distance between nasal base and midline upper lip vermilion border more than 2 SD above the mean. Alternatively, an apparently increased distance between nasal base and midline upper lip vermilion border.

HP:0000369.name: Low-set ears
HP:0000369.definition: Upper insertion of the ear to the scalp below an imaginary horizontal line drawn between the inner canthi of the eye and extending posteriorly to the ear.

HP:0000670.name: Carious teeth
HP:0000670.definition: Caries is a multifactorial bacterial infection affecting the structure of the tooth. This term has been used to describe the presence of more than expected dental caries.

HP:0000689.name: Dental malocclusion
HP:0000689.definition: Dental malocclusion refers to an abnormality of the occlusion, or alignment, of the teeth and the way the upper and lower teeth fit together, resulting in overcrowding of teeth or in abnormal bite patterns.

HP:0000707.name: Abnormality of the nervous system
HP:0000707.definition: An abnormality of the nervous system.

HP:0000717.name: Autism
HP:0000717.definition: Autism is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by impaired social interaction and communication, and by restricted and repetitive behavior. Autism begins in childhood. HP:0000729.name: Autistic behavior
HP:0000729.definition: Persistent deficits in social interaction and communication and interaction as well as a markedly restricted repertoire of activity and interest as well as repetitive patterns of behavior.

HP:0000733.name: Motor stereotypy
HP:0000733.definition: Use of the same abnormal action in response to certain triggers or at random. They may be used as a way to regulate one's internal state but must otherwise have no apparent functional purpose.

HP:0000750.name: Delayed speech and language development
HP:0000750.definition: A degree of language development that is significantly below the norm for a child of a specified age.

HP:0000807.name: Glanular hypospadias
HP:0000807.definition: A type of hypospadias in which the urethral meatus is located at the head of the penis, but not all the way at the tip.

HP:0000924.name: Abnormality of the skeletal system
HP:0000924.definition: An abnormality of the skeletal system.

HP:0001263.name: Global developmental delay
HP:0001263.definition: A delay in the achievement of motor or mental milestones in the domains of development of a child, including motor skills, speech and language, cognitive skills, and social and emotional skills. This term should only be used to describe children younger than five years of age.

HP:0001270.name: Motor delay
HP:0001270.definition: A type of Developmental delay characterized by a delay in acquiring motor skills.
synonyms: Delay in development of motor milestones

HP:0001274.name: Agenesis of corpus callosum
HP:0001274.definition: Absence of the corpus callosum as a result of the failure of the corpus callosum to develop, which can be the result of a failure in any one of the multiple steps of callosal development including cellular proliferation and migration, axonal growth or glial patterning at the midline.

HP:0001511.name: Intrauterine growth retardation
HP:0001511.definition: An abnormal restriction of fetal growth with fetal weight below the tenth percentile for gestational age.

HP:0001642.name: Pulmonic stenosis
HP:0001642.definition: A narrowing of the right ventricular outflow tract that can occur at the pulmonary valve (valvular stenosis), below the pulmonary valve (infundibular stenosis), or above the pulmonary valve (supravalvar stenosis).

HP:0001999.name: Abnormal facial shape
HP:0001999.definition: An abnormal morphology (form) of the face or its components.

HP:0002463.name: Language impairment
HP:0002463.definition: Language impairment is a deficit in comprehension or production of language that includes reduced vocabulary, limited sentence structure, or impairments in written or spoken communication. Language abilities are substantially and quantifiably below age expectations.

HP:0002721.name: Immunodeficiency
HP:0002721.definition: Failure of the immune system to protect the body adequately from infection, due to the absence or insufficiency of some component process or substance.

HP:0003765.name: Psoriasiform dermatitis
HP:0003765.definition: A skin abnormality characterized by redness and irritation, with thick, red skin that displays flaky, silver-white patches (scales).

HP:0004430.name: Severe combined immunodeficiency
HP:0004430.definition: A type of primary immune deficiency that is characterized by a more severe defect in both the T- and B-lymphocyte systems.

HP:0007018.name: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder
HP:0007018.definition: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) manifests at age 2-3 years or by first grade at the latest. HP:0010783.name: Erythema
HP:0010783.definition: Redness of the skin, caused by hyperemia of the capillaries in the lower layers of the skin.
synonyms: Redness of skin or mucous membrane

HP:0011410.name: Caesarean section
HP:0011410.definition: Delivery of a fetus through surgical incisions made through the abdominal wall (laparotomy) and the uterine wall (hysterotomy).

HP:0012535.name: Abnormal synaptic transmission
HP:0012535.definition: An anomaly in the communication from a neuron to a target across a synapse. HP:0012758.name: Neurodevelopmental delay

HP:0012759.name: Neurodevelopmental abnormality
HP:0012759.definition: A deviation from normal of the neurological development of a child, which may include any or all of the aspects of the development of personal, social, gross or fine motor, and cognitive abilities.

HP:0030680.name: Abnormal cardiovascular system morphology
HP:0030680.definition: Any structural anomaly of the heart and blood vessels.

HP:0100699.name: Scarring
HP:0100699.definition: A scar refers to a lesion in which wound, burn, or sore has not healed completely and fibrous connective tissue has developed.

HP:0000358.name: Posteriorly rotated ears
HP:0000358.definition: A type of abnormal location of the ears in which the position of the ears is characterized by posterior rotation (the superior part of the ears is rotated towards the back of the head, and the inferior part of the ears towards the front).
synonyms: Ears rotated toward back of head

HP:0000365.name: Hearing impairment
HP:0000365.definition: A decreased magnitude of the sensory perception of sound.

HP:0000407.name: Sensorineural hearing impairment
HP:0000407.definition: A type of hearing impairment in one or both ears related to an abnormal functionality of the cochlear nerve.

HP:0000478.name: Abnormality of the eye
HP:0000478.definition: Any abnormality of the eye, including location, spacing, and intraocular abnormalities.

HP:0000482.name: Microcornea
HP:0000482.definition: A congenital abnormality of the cornea in which the cornea and the anterior segment of the eye are smaller than normal. The horizontal diameter of the cornea does not reach 10 mm even in adulthood.
synonyms: Cornea of eye less than 10mm in diameter

HP:0000494.name: Downslanted palpebral fissures
HP:0000494.definition: The palpebral fissure inclination is more than two standard deviations below the mean.

HP:0000501.name: Glaucoma
HP:0000501.definition: Glaucoma refers loss of retinal ganglion cells in a characteristic pattern of optic neuropathy usually associated with increased intraocular pressure.

HP:0000505.name: Visual impairment

HP:0000518.name: Cataract
HP:0000518.definition: A cataract is an opacity or clouding that develops in the crystalline lens of the eye or in its capsule.
synonyms: Clouding of the lens of the eye

HP:0000519.name: Developmental cataract
HP:0000519.definition: A cataract that occurs congenitally as the result of a developmental defect, in contrast to the majority of cataracts that occur in adulthood as the result of degenerative changes of the lens.
synonyms: Clouding of the lens of the eye at birth

HP:0000568.name: Microphthalmia
HP:0000568.definition: A developmental anomaly characterized by abnormal smallness of one or both eyes.

HP:0000689.name: Dental malocclusion
HP:0000689.definition: Dental malocclusion refers to an abnormality of the occlusion, or alignment, of the teeth and the way the upper and lower teeth fit together, resulting in overcrowding of teeth or in abnormal bite patterns.

HP:0000729.name: Autistic behavior
HP:0000729.definition: Persistent deficits in social interaction and communication and interaction as well as a markedly restricted repertoire of activity and interest as well as repetitive patterns of behavior.

HP:0000924.name: Abnormality of the skeletal system
HP:0000924.definition: An abnormality of the skeletal system.

HP:0001141.definition: Severe reduction of the ability to see. On the 6m visual acuity scale, severe reduction is defined as less than 6/60 but at least 3/60. HP:0001250.name: Seizure
HP:0001250.definition: A seizure is an intermittent abnormality of nervous system physiology characterized by a transient occurrence of signs and/or symptoms due to abnormal excessive or synchronous neuronal activity in the brain.

HP:0001256.name: Mild intellectual disability
HP:0001256.definition: Mild intellectual disability (ID) is defined as a type of ID characterized by mildly sub-average adaptive functioning and intellectual functioning, with an intelligence quotient (IQ) the range of 50-69.

HP:0001263.name: Global developmental delay
HP:0001263.definition: A delay in the achievement of motor or mental milestones in the domains of development of a child, including motor skills, speech and language, cognitive skills, and social and emotional skills. This term should only be used to describe children younger than five years of age.

HP:0001328.name: Specific learning disability
HP:0001328.definition: Impairment of certain skills such as reading or writing, coordination, self-control, or attention that interfere with the ability to learn. The impairment is not related to a global deficiency of intelligence.

HP:0001596.name: Alopecia
HP:0001596.definition: A noncongenital process of hair loss, which may progress to partial or complete baldness.

HP:0001999.name: Abnormal facial shape
HP:0001999.definition: An abnormal morphology (form) of the face or its components.

HP:0002353.name: EEG abnormality
HP:0002353.definition: Abnormality observed by electroencephalogram (EEG), which is used to record of the brain's spontaneous electrical activity from multiple electrodes placed on the scalp.

HP:0002650.name: Scoliosis
HP:0002650.definition: The presence of an abnormal lateral curvature of the spine.
synonyms: Cobb angle greater than ten degrees

HP:0004322.name: Short stature
HP:0004322.definition: A height below that which is expected according to age and gender norms. HP:0004395.name: Malnutrition
HP:0004395.definition: A deficiency in the intake of energy and nutrients.

HP:0007700.name: Ocular anterior segment dysgenesis
HP:0007700.definition: Abnormal development (dysgenesis) of the anterior segment of the eye globe. These structures are mainly of mesenchymal origin.

HP:0007834.name: Progressive cataract
HP:0007834.definition: A kind of cataract that progresses with age.

HP:0007971.name: Lamellar cataract
HP:0007971.definition: A congenital cataract in which opacity is limited to layers of the lens external to the nucleus (i.e., the perinuclear region), i.e., between the nuclear and cortical layers of the lens.

HP:0010698.name: Nuclear pulverulent cataract
HP:0010698.definition: A type of nuclear cataract involving congenital dust-like (pulverulent) opacity of the embryonal and fetal nucleus.

HP:0011502.name: Posterior lenticonus
HP:0011502.definition: A conical projection of the posterior surface of the lens, occurring as a developmental anomaly.

HP:0012368.name: Flat face
HP:0012368.definition: Absence of concavity or convexity of the face when viewed in profile.

HP:0100244.name: Fibrosarcoma
HP:0100244.definition: A fibroblastic sarcoma is a malignant tumor derived from fibrous connective tissue and characterized by immature proliferating fibroblasts or undifferentiated anaplastic spindle cells.

HP:0001250.name: Seizure
HP:0001250.definition: A seizure is an intermittent abnormality of nervous system physiology characterized by a transient occurrence of signs and/or symptoms due to abnormal excessive or synchronous neuronal activity in the brain.

HP:0001251.name: Ataxia
HP:0001251.definition: Ataxia refers to impaired coordination of voluntary muscle movement. Cerebellar ataxia refers to ataxia due to dysfunction of the cerebellum. HP:0001252.name: Hypotonia

HP:0001257.name: Spasticity
HP:0001257.definition: A motor disorder characterized by a velocity-dependent increase in tonic stretch reflexes with increased muscle tone, exaggerated (hyperexcitable) tendon reflexes.
synonyms: Involuntary muscle stiffness, contraction, or spasm

HP:0001258.name: Spastic paraplegia
HP:0001258.definition: Complete loss of the ability to move the lower limbs accompanied by spasticity of the lower limbs.

HP:0001260.name: Dysarthria
HP:0001260.definition: Dysarthric speech is a general description referring to a neurological speech disorder characterized by poor articulation. Depending on the involved neurological structures, dysarthria may be further classified as spastic, flaccid, ataxic, hyperkinetic and hypokinetic, or mixed.

HP:0001263.name: Global developmental delay
HP:0001263.definition: A delay in the achievement of motor or mental milestones in the domains of development of a child, including motor skills, speech and language, cognitive skills, and social and emotional skills. This term should only be used to describe children younger than five years of age.

HP:0001268.name: Mental deterioration
HP:0001268.definition: Loss of previously present mental abilities, generally in adults.

HP:0001270.name: Motor delay
HP:0001270.definition: A type of Developmental delay characterized by a delay in acquiring motor skills.
synonyms: Delay in development of motor milestones

HP:0001272.name: Cerebellar atrophy
HP:0001272.definition: Cerebellar atrophy is defined as a cerebellum with initially normal structures, in a posterior fossa with normal size, which displays enlarged fissures (interfolial spaces) in comparison to the foliae secondary to loss of tissue. HP:0001332.name: Dystonia
HP:0001332.definition: An abnormally increased muscular tone that causes fixed abnormal postures. There is a slow, intermittent twisting motion that leads to exaggerated turning and posture of the extremities and trunk.

HP:0001348.name: Brisk reflexes
HP:0001348.definition: Tendon reflexes that are noticeably more active than usual (conventionally denoted 3+ on clinical examination). Brisk reflexes may or may not indicate a neurological lesion. HP:0002066.name: Gait ataxia
HP:0002066.definition: A type of ataxia characterized by the impairment of the ability to coordinate the movements required for normal walking. Gait ataxia is characteirzed by a wide-based staggering gait with a tendency to fall.
synonyms: Inability to coordinate movements when walking

HP:0002070.name: Limb ataxia
HP:0002070.definition: A kind of ataxia that affects movements of the extremities.

HP:0002191.name: Progressive spasticity
HP:0002191.definition: Spasticity that increases in degree with time.

HP:0002311.name: Incoordination
HP:0002311.definition: A deficit in coordination of muscle movements. Coordination is defined as the orchestrated movement of multiple body parts as required to accomplish intended actions, like walking.

HP:0002415.name: Leukodystrophy
HP:0002415.definition: Leukodystrophy refers to deterioration of white matter of the brain resulting from degeneration of myelin sheaths in the CNS.
